The ability to perform transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) is influenced by the surgeon's previous experience. According to our retrieved matches, senior urologists who have more experience tend to be capable of performing TURP with greater efficiency, with some studies suggesting that they can resect four times more tissue per time unit compared to less experienced surgeons.

This increased proficiency allows them to better manage and complete the procedure with fewer complications. However, it's essential to note that while experience may play a role in improving outcomes, other factors such as the patient's overall health, preoperative features, and stage of cancer also influence the success of TURP.

Therefore, surgeons' previous experience is an important consideration when evaluating their ability to perform TURP. It's crucial for urologists to consider their own experiences and those of their colleagues when assessing a surgeon's capabilities before performing a complex procedure like TURP.
